issues.title: The accessible name (from the link’s text), together with the absence of programmatically determined link context, does not describe the purpose of the link.
issues.why_it_matters_for_persona: As an autistic person, ambiguous links like 'More' are a significant source of anxiety and cognitive friction. I need to know exactly where a link will take me before I click it to maintain a predictable browsing experience. When I see a generic link, I have to stop and read the surrounding text to figure out its purpose, which breaks my concentration and adds unnecessary mental effort.
remediation_instructions: Make the link text more descriptive so that its purpose can be understood from the link text alone. For example: `More about this product`.
Alternatively, use an `aria-label` to provide a more descriptive accessible name for the link, while keeping the visible text short. For example: `More`.
Another option is to programmatically associate the descriptive text with the link using `aria-describedby`. For example: `More`.
expected_tool_change: An automated accessibility checker will likely flag the link for using common, ambiguous link text like 'More'.
After fixing, a screen reader will announce a descriptive name (e.g., 'More about this product, link') instead of just 'More, link'.
